newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia threatens tax debtor firms with bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Russia threatens tax debtor firms with bankruptcy.

text.p: Russia on Tuesday threatened to begin bankruptcy proceedings against six big companies, including oil giants AO Tatneft TATN.RTS and AO Purneftegaz PFGS.RTS, unless they paid their taxes within a week.
A government commission on payments said in a statement it had examined the financial situation of a number of big tax debtors.
"The result of this is a decision to start bankruptcy cases against a number of the biggest tax dodgers which systematically pay less than 20 percent of current taxes," the statement said.
The companies, which also included car maker AO Kamaz KMAZ.RTS, had been told to pay tax arrears within a week from October 14, or the cases would be sent to arbitration court.
The other companies named were car maker AO Moskvich, oil refiner AO Krasnodarnefteorgsintez and alumina company AO Achinsky Glinozyomny Kombinat.
The statement said the position of 10 other companies was being examined.

It said tax arrears in the first eight months of the year were more than 50 trillion roubles ($9.2 billion) and that state coffers received just 79 percent of budgeted taxes. ($ = 5440 Russian Roubles)
